def starts_one_ends(n):
    if n == 1:
        return 1  # Only the single digit 1 meets the criteria

    # Count of numbers starting with 1
    start_with_1 = 9**(n-1)
    
    # Count of numbers ending with 1
    end_with_1 = 9**(n-1)
    
    # When n > 1, numbers like 11, 101, 1001, ..., which start and end with 1 are counted twice
    start_and_end_with_1 = 9**(n-2) if n > 2 else 1
    
    return start_with_1 + end_with_1 - start_and_end_with_1

def starts_one_ends(n):
    if n == 1:
        return 1  # The single digit 1 itself
    else:
        # Count numbers starting with 1: 1 followed by (n-1) digits, each can be 0-9
        count_starts_with_1 = 10**(n-1)
        # Count numbers ending with 1: (first n-1 digits can be anything but the last one is 1)
        count_ends_with_1 = 10**(n-1)
        # Overcounted numbers starting and ending with 1: 1 followed by (n-2) digits, each can be 0-9, then 1
        count_starts_and_ends_with_1 = 10**(n-2)
        return count_starts_with_1 + count_ends_with_1 - count_starts_and_ends_with_1
